numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For ElasticNetCV(positive=True) and LassoCV(positive=True), alpha_max (the first alpha in the grid) is computed incorrectly; the alpha search range is wrong. With the reproducer's alpha_min=np.float64(2.0), ElasticNet(alpha=alpha_min, fit_intercept=False, positive=True).fit(X, y).coef_.max() is 0 (all coefficients zero) instead of > 0; the assertion 'alpha_min still gives all zero coef' fails. In the PR test, ElasticNetCV(alphas=1, cv=2, eps=1, fit_intercept=False, positive=True).alpha_ equals np.float64(66.63636363636364), which is wrong because the positive constraint is ignored when computing X.T @ wy (unconstrained gives [733., -476.] instead of the non-negative-aware values).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: alpha_max should be correct for positive=True so that ElasticNet at alpha_max gives all-zero coefficients and ElasticNet at alpha_min (the smallest grid alpha) gives at least one nonzero coefficient (coef_.max() > 0). The positive constraint should be respected when computing alpha_max, e.g. by clipping Xyw with np.maximum(0, Xyw) when positive is True.
trigger_conditions: positive=True passed to ElasticNetCV or LassoCV
sample_weight used in the PR test (np.array([1, 10, 1, 10]) or None)
X has negative-correlated columns so that Xy has negative entries that the positive constraint should clip
enet_path did not forward positive to _alpha_grid before the fix

input_output_examples.input: X = np.array([[1, 1], [1, -1]]); beta = np.array([1, -1e3]); y = X @ beta; config = dict(fit_intercept=False, positive=True); ElasticNet(alpha=alpha_min, **config).fit(X, y).coef_.max() where alpha_min = alphas_[-1] from ElasticNetCV(cv=2, **config)
ElasticNetCV(alphas=1, cv=2, eps=1, fit_intercept=False, positive=True).fit(X, y) with X = [[3,-1],[2,-5],[5,-3],[1,-4]], beta=[1,-2], sample_weight=[1,10,1,10]
input_output_examples.expected_output: a value that makes coefficients zero at alpha_max for positive=True (test asserts alpha_max correctness; exact expected value not given in passages)

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: alpha_max=np.float64(2000.0), alpha_min=np.float64(2.0) from issue #32767 reproducer; y built from beta=[1,-1e3]
category_specific_evidence: Issue #32767 reproducer: ElasticNet(alpha=alpha_max, fit_intercept=False, positive=True) gives all-zero coef as expected (assert coef_.max()==0 passes), but ElasticNet(alpha=alpha_min) still gives all-zero coef (AssertionError: alpha_min=np.float64(2.0) still gives all zero coef), violating the property that alpha_min from the ElasticNetCV grid should yield a nonzero solution.
Fix PR #32768 states: make alpha_max and the alpha search range correct for ElasticNetCV(positive=True) and LassoCV(positive=True).

Test failure in test_enet_alpha_max: ElasticNetCV(alphas=1, cv=2, eps=1, fit_intercept=False, positive=True).alpha_ returned np.float64(66.63636363636364) where alpha_max should make coefs zero; X.T @ wy changed from [733., -476.] (old, negative columns) to [733., 476.] after the test's X was sign-flipped, showing the positive-constrained gradient should use the nonnegative direction.
enet_path call was missing positive=positive argument, which the diff adds.
reproduction_risks: Exact floating-point equality is used in the issue reproducer (coef_.max() == 0), so rounding could matter.
The reproducer depends on alphas_ grid from ElasticNetCV(cv=2), so alpha_min/alpha_max values depend on that grid.
MultiTaskElasticNetCV has no positive attribute; the fix uses getattr(self, 'positive', False), so tests must not assume positive exists there.
